description: Deploys a MULTI-CONTAINER app - a repo that ships docker-compose.yml / compose.yaml - onto ONE VM via podman-compose, and exposes one or more services at redu.cloud URLs. Use this instead of deploy_app when the repo is a compose stack. Same prereqs + source modes as deploy_app; always run plan_deploy first. PORT is the HOST port for the exposed service. DATASTORES ARE MANAGED BY DEFAULT: each one you reported in send_signals runs as a managed store; the stack keeps its own settings, and its own copy of each store is replaced by a forwarder of the same name to the managed one (the stack's own user, password and database created there, its init scripts run once). Pass no database/redis/qdrant settings; 'compose' (the stack's own) only when the user asked for one VM. For WordPress/WooCommerce cluster intent, do not leave the compose db service/local uploads as state: pass app_profile, cluster_target:true, database:'managed', db_engine:'mariadb' or 'mysql', cluster_media_mode:'media_space', and either media_space_id or create_media_space:true. Redu writes an override file that points the WordPress service at managed DB env and mounts the media space into /var/www/html/wp-content/uploads. Poll get_deployment until ready.

app_profile.description: Detected app profile from source inspection. For WordPress/WooCommerce pass wordpress/woocommerce so cluster deploys enforce managed DB + shared media instead of treating local uploads as stateless.

approved.description: ONLY when send_signals said approval_required (this account approves before anything paid starts): true after the USER said yes to the plan and its cost in this conversation. Never set it yourself, and leave it out in every other case.

cluster_media_mode.description: Record the WordPress media strategy for future clustering. For real WordPress clusters use media_space by default: Redu mounts a shared uploads filesystem into every member. local_uploads is single-VM only and upgrade_to_cluster will refuse it for WordPress.

cluster_target.description: Set TRUE when the user asked to deploy this compose app as an autoscaling cluster. For WordPress/WooCommerce this requires managed MySQL/MariaDB plus media_space/central_media_origin.

compose_engine.description: Container engine for the compose build (default: the server's choice, usually podman). Set 'docker' to force the docker engine.

compose_file.description: Path within the source to the compose file (e.g. 'deploy/docker-compose.yml'). Auto-detected (docker-compose.yml / compose.yaml / …) if omitted.

create_media_space.description: For WordPress/WooCommerce cluster_target:true: set TRUE when no suitable media space exists. Redu creates an NFS media VM + persistent volume and mounts it into /var/www/html/wp-content/uploads.

database.description: DB mode: 'managed' = a SEPARATE managed Postgres/MySQL/MariaDB VM. THE STACK KEEPS ITS OWN SETTINGS: its own copy of the store (a service running that store's image) is replaced by a forwarder under the same name, the stack's own user, password and database are created on the managed store and its init scripts run once; a store the stack has no copy of gets DATABASE_URL/PG*/MYSQL_* appended to the project .env. 'compose' = the stack's own db service (without a signal the default; with one, only when the user asked for one VM); 'single_vm' = Postgres ON the app VM. Your compose file is never rewritten.

db_engine.description: managed only: 'postgres' (default) → PG* env; 'mysql'/'mariadb' → MYSQL_* env. mysql/mariadb require database:'managed'.

db_extensions.description: single_vm/managed Postgres: extensions to pre-install (pgvector, postgis, pgaudit, …).

db_flavor_id.description: managed only: the dedicated DB VM size (from list_flavors). Defaults to the app flavor.

db_superuser.description: single_vm/managed Postgres: grant the DB user SUPERUSER (dedicated DB VM, so safe).

db_version.description: DB version for single_vm/managed (Postgres '16'|'15'|'14'; MySQL '8.0'; MariaDB '11.4').

dname.description: Custom *.redu.cloud subdomain. For a STABLE, KNOWN-AHEAD URL (needed when the app must be told its OWN url - OAuth callbacks, cookie domain, a frontend that calls its API), generate the FULL auto-gen form yourself: `<label>-<8 lowercase letters/digits>.redu.cloud` (e.g. `myapp-7k2m9x4p.redu.cloud`) - that exact form is used VERBATIM - and wire the app's own URL env to that SAME value. A BARE `<label>.redu.cloud` is NOT used as-is: redu appends a random 8-char suffix for uniqueness, so anything wired to the bare name will NOT match the real URL. Omit to auto-generate (then read the real URL from get_deployment).

env.description: Env vars APPENDED to the compose project's .env (for ${VAR} interpolation). We never rewrite your compose file.

expose.description: MULTI-SURFACE apps: expose several services, each gets its OWN *.redu.cloud URL. The FIRST entry is the primary one redu health-gates (its port overrides `port`). CRITICAL when one surface must KNOW another's URL (a frontend that calls its API - e.g. Lago's front -> API): GENERATE each surface's dname up front as `<label>-<8 lowercase letters/digits>.redu.cloud` (used VERBATIM) and wire the app's cross-surface URL env (LAGO_API_URL, LAGO_FRONT_URL, FRONTEND_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL, …) to those EXACT values. Do NOT use a bare `<label>.redu.cloud` - redu appends a random suffix, so config wired to the bare name breaks.

flavor_id.description: App VM size - from list_flavors. A multi-container stack often wants m1.large+; plan_deploy sizes it.

git_ref.description: git mode only: branch/tag/commit (default: the repo's default branch).

git_token.description: git mode only: token to clone a PRIVATE repo.

keypair_name.description: REQUIRED. An EXISTING SSH keypair name - from list_keypairs / import_keypair.

machine_id.description: EXPERIMENT: the prepared machine to run this deploy on, from prepare_machine. Omit: the newest one this session has not used yet.

media_mount_path.description: Host mount path on the app VM/member. Redu mounts this into /var/www/html/wp-content/uploads.

media_origin_url.description: Public base URL where WordPress wp-content/uploads is served when using central_media_origin. Do not put this on the DB VM.

media_space_flavor_id.description: Flavor id for the media VM when create_media_space:true. Defaults to m1.small/backend default.

media_space_id.description: Existing Redu media space id to mount at WordPress wp-content/uploads. Get it from list_media_spaces.

media_space_name.description: Optional media space name when create_media_space:true. Defaults to <deployment-name>-media.

media_space_size_gb.description: Media space data volume size in GB when create_media_space:true (default 20).

migrate_command.description: One-time DB prepare/migrate/seed, run AFTER `up -d` and BEFORE the app is marked ready - redu runs `podman-compose run --rm <migrate_service|service> <cmd>` (Rails `bundle exec rails db:prepare`, Django `python manage.py migrate`, Prisma `prisma migrate deploy`). REQUIRED for any stack whose schema is NOT auto-created on boot (e.g. Lago): WITHOUT it the stack deploys and flips to 'ready' but 502s on real use because the DB schema is missing.

migrate_service.description: Compose service to run migrate_command in (defaults to `service`).

name.description: Name for the deployment / VM (lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens).

network_id.description: Private network id - auto-selected from check_deploy_prerequisites if omitted.

port.description: REQUIRED in practice: the HOST port the exposed service publishes (the LEFT side of its compose `ports:` mapping) - redu health-probes + proxies THIS port, so a wrong value fails the deploy. plan_deploy detects it.

qdrant.description: 'managed' = a managed Qdrant: the stack's own qdrant service is replaced by a forwarder of the same name that adds the managed API key, or QDRANT_URL/QDRANT_API_KEY is appended when the stack has none. 'none' keeps the stack's own qdrant.

qdrant_flavor_id.description: managed Qdrant only: the Qdrant VM size (from list_flavors).

redis.description: 'managed' = a SEPARATE managed Redis VM: the stack's own redis service is replaced by a forwarder of the same name that authenticates to it (the managed Redis always has a password; the stack's own AUTH, if any, is answered for it), or REDIS_URL/REDIS_* is appended when the stack has no redis. 'none' keeps the stack's own redis.

redis_flavor_id.description: managed Redis only: the dedicated Redis VM size (from list_flavors). Defaults to the app flavor.

redis_password.description: managed Redis only: a specific password to set (otherwise auto-generated).

repo.description: Filled in for you with the repository URL the USER gave (url_given_by_user in send_signals); the VM clones it. Otherwise omit it and pass source_token: the folder you work in is the source. Private repo also needs git_token.

service.description: The compose SERVICE to expose at the public URL (informational; the exposed port is `port`).

source_token.description: UPLOAD MODE: token from prepare_upload - deploys an uploaded tarball of your LOCAL dir (no git). Omit `repo` when set.

subdir.description: Directory within the source that contains the compose file (if not at the root).

name: deploy_compose
title: Deploy a docker-compose (multi-container) app to a VM
